Typical hourly pedestrian counts by sensor, year and day type

Source: R/data.R
ped_hourly.Rd

Average pedestrian counts for each hour of the day, summarised from the City of Melbourne Pedestrian Counting System (counts per hour). Each row is the average count in one hour of the day, for one sensor location, in one year, on weekdays or on weekends. Hours with fewer than 10 recorded days were dropped to avoid noisy averages.

Usage

ped_hourly

Format

A data frame (tibble) with one row per sensor, year, day type and hour, and these columns:

location_id

Integer ID of the sensor location. Matches location_id in ped_sensors.

sensor_name

Short name of the sensor location, for example a street or mall name.

year

Calendar year (integer).

day_type

Either "Weekday" (Monday to Friday) or "Weekend" (Saturday and Sunday).

hour

Hour of the day, from 0 (midnight to 1am) to 23 (11pm to midnight).

mean_count

Average number of pedestrians counted in that hour, across all recorded days in that group, rounded to one decimal place.

n_days

Number of distinct days that went into the average. Small values mean the sensor was working for only part of the year, so treat the average with more caution.

Source

City of Melbourne, Pedestrian Counting System (counts per hour), City of Melbourne Open Data Portal, https://data.melbourne.vic.gov.au/explore/dataset/pedestrian-counting-system-monthly-counts-per-hour/. The portal page for this dataset does not state a licence. The companion Sensor Locations dataset is licensed CC BY 4.0, so attribution to the City of Melbourne is given here.

Details

Every year covers the same stretch of the calendar, from 1 January to 2 November, so years can be compared without seasonal differences. Earlier parts of the data that did not span a whole January to November window (late 2024) and dates after 2 November are not included.

The data are prepared by data-raw/ped_data.R.

Examples

head(ped_hourly)
#> # A tibble: 6 × 7
#>   location_id sensor_name  year day_type  hour mean_count n_days
#>         <int> <chr>       <int> <chr>    <int>      <dbl>  <int>
#> 1         108 261Will_T    2025 Weekday      0       56.3    218
#> 2         108 261Will_T    2025 Weekday      1       30.1    218
#> 3         108 261Will_T    2025 Weekday      2       19.7    218
#> 4         108 261Will_T    2025 Weekday      3       14.5    218
#> 5         108 261Will_T    2025 Weekday      4       14.2    217
#> 6         108 261Will_T    2025 Weekday      5       83.1    218
